items.headline: 湖名之爭：加拿大回敬川普
items.context: 美國總統川普想把安大略湖改稱「美國湖」，安大略省長福特（Doug Ford）豎起巨大看板反擊，寫著「安大略湖，現在與永遠都是」。Google 地圖證實，會依美國政府決定，把美國使用者看到的名稱改掉，但加拿大使用者看到的仍是安大略湖。
items.thread_text: 美國總統川普想把安大略湖改名「美國湖」，安大略省長福特（Doug Ford）在湖邊立起巨大看板反擊，寫著「安大略湖，現在與永遠都是」。Google 地圖證實，美國使用者看到的名稱會依美國政府決定更改，但加拿大使用者看到的名字不變。本則整理自 BBC、NPR 與半島電視台報導。
items.threads_text: 這場地圖上的湖名之爭越演越烈。美國總統川普想把安大略湖改稱「美國湖」，安大略省長福特（Doug Ford）不甘示弱，在湖邊立起巨大看板，寫著「安大略湖，現在與永遠都是」。更妙的是 Google 地圖也捲入戰局——公司證實，美國使用者之後會看到新名字，但加拿大使用者看到的名稱不受影響。一場政治口水戰，硬是打到了地圖圖層上。本則整理自 BBC、NPR 與半島電視台報導。

sources.summary: Pleasance Courtyard, Edinburgh The comic’s unique tale of assimilation and romance-related limbo has a high joke rate and emotional intelligence I want to tell Omar Badawy to take a breath. This debut moves at a frantic, almost dizzying pace, so much so that you could easily miss a few details in a show that zooms in and out of the time he was accidentally caught in the middle of a Tommy Robinson march while en route to a fancy dress party. But with writing this sharp, does it matter? You can see why SNL: UK came calling. The Cambridge-raised Badawy lays out his identity conundrum: he’s an Anglo-Egyptian Muslim who, as a pupil at a Christian school, was teased for his background. Differences surfaced during Nativity plays, where his culturally accurate interpretations of innkeepers and wise men’s assistants weren’t quite what his teachers had in mind. He also knows his well-spoken accent makes it easier to assimilate. Because of all this, Badawy often feels stuck in the middle. Once, a stranger even asked his ethnicity because he wanted to call him his “correct racial slur”. sources.summary: Edinburgh Playhouse San Francisco Ballet brings a spectacular collision of dance, music and digital wizardry to the Edinburgh international festival in this bold reimagining of Pandora’s box This is a spectacular show. Literally, it is full of spectacle: as much a visual extravaganza as it is a concert, as it is dance – and a gloriously maddening piece of dance at that. The dancers are as impressive as you’d expect from San Francisco Ballet, the US’s oldest professional ballet company, and the splashy concept is bold: artistic director Tamara Rojo commissioned choreographer Aszure Barton, composer Sam Shepherd (AKA electronic producer Floating Points) and multidisciplinary artists Hamill Industries, their starting point being the myth of Pandora’s box, transposed to the current world of AI technology and what unknowns we might be unleashing. Hamill Industries, who used some AI in their creation process, unleash something transfixing on a giant screen above the stage: morphing, pulsating pixels that look like lava or the surface of the sun. It’s intoxicating, easily dragging attention away from the dancers’ bodies (this may be the whole point – more on this later). Those dancers appear en masse in strict manoeuvres at driving tempo. Are they an army of mortals, gods, automatons or lines of code? Who knows. But they are moulded into large-scale moving images by Barton just as Pandora is moulded from clay in the best bit of integration between the digital and physical worlds, countless hands crafting this first woman out of dust. Barton is a magpie of a choreographer, always unpredictable, classical virtuosity sewn in among countless other ideas in unstoppable phrases. Jennifer Stahl as Pandora is an impressive creation, for sure, and Wei Wang is great: supple, sprightly, puckish. He represents Hope, although you wouldn’t know that without doing a bit of research. Choreographers are not duty-bound to enact a narrative; the Pandora tale is merely a creative trigger, they’d say, but in a story with such clear dramatic beats, and such a clever contemporary parallel, it does seem a waste to essentially throw that away. Continue reading...

sources.summary: Stavroula Adameitis, AKA Frida Las Vegas, is an Adelaide-based artist and designer known for her camp, pop art aesthetic. A typical work might feature palm trees, poodles, Greek pillars or bin chickens (Australian white ibises), sometimes all at once. Does it veer into kitsch? ‘I hope so,’ she says. ‘Nostalgia, colour and fun can be very energising, and the feeling we get from these objects in popular culture binds us together.’ The term kitsch comes from the German verkitschen, meaning ‘to cheapen’. In the 19th century it was deployed by elites to look down on the supposedly trashy vulgarity of art for the masses. ‘The idea still carries negative connotations,’ says Adameitis. In her new book, she invites us to stop sneering and start relishing Australia’s unparalleled genius for kitsch: ‘Good kitsch laughs with you not at you. It brings people along for the ride.’ Continue reading...

items.context: 《衛報》社論指出，中國掌控全球約七成稀土礦產與九成的分離加工，這個問題自 2010 年中國因島嶼爭端一度封鎖對日稀土出口就已經敲響警鐘，但外界始終沒有真正採取行動。
items.thread_text: 《衛報》社論談稀土供應鏈，這篇是編輯部的觀點文章。文中指出，中國掌控全球約七成稀土礦產與九成的分離加工，這個警訊早在 2010 年中國一度封鎖對日稀土出口時就已經響起，但外界始終沒有真正採取行動。這場為期一年的貿易休兵，將在 11 月到期。目前這則消息只有《衛報》報導。
items.threads_text: 這是《衛報》編輯部的一篇社論，談的是稀土供應鏈的戰略問題。文中指出，中國掌控全球約七成稀土礦產與九成的分離加工能力，這個警訊早在 2010 年——中國因為島嶼爭端一度封鎖對日稀土出口時——就已經響起，但外界始終沒有真正採取行動。去年北京正是靠收緊稀土出口，逼美國總統川普從貿易戰中退讓，而不是靠報復性關稅。這場為期一年的貿易休兵，將在 11 月到期，通訊設施關鍵原料「鉺」的價格，已經因為市場擔心出口管制重啟而上漲。這篇社論的立場是：把稀土產業外包給中國，已經到了不能再繼續的地步。目前這則消息只有《衛報》報導。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Outsourcing the industry to China cannot continue, but Europe knows it can no longer count on the US for a solution The alarm sounded 16 years ago. In 2010, China blocked exports of key rare earths to Japan in a row over disputed islands in the East China Sea. The critical minerals are essential to everything from advanced weaponry and iPhones to electric vehicle batteries and wind turbines, so the rest of the world took note. But it didn’t take much action. China still accounts for about 70% of rare-earth mining globally and 90% of separation and processing. Then, last year, Beijing forced Donald Trump to back away from his trade war – not with its retaliatory tariffs, but the curbing of rare-earth exports. A scramble for new supplies began in earnest. The year-long trade truce is due to expire in November. The price of erbium, an element essential to communications infrastructure, has already jumped because of fears that export controls will soon be renewed. Continue reading...
